title: The finite-extension incomparability construction uses a stale target length and repeats the same diagonal bit.
details: Marks, version2024-02-25, Theorem18.1 proof, printed/PDF pp.74–75. At stage2n+1 the current target prefix is t_(2n), but m is defined as |t_n|; it must be |t_(2n)| to designate an unset target bit. In Case1 both output branches append1 to t_(2n). Append1 when the finite oracle output is0 and append0 otherwise; this differs from the source’s Booleanized output in either case. The chosen successful extension s* need not strictly extend s_(2n), despite the announced strict length growth; append a harmless bit to s* if necessary, using preservation of a successful finite-oracle computation under extension. Switch source and target at the even stage. These local changes ensure unbounded lengths, persistent diagonal disagreement and the claimed incomparability. Theorem18.2’s halting-oracle choice argument then computes the corrected sequence. The p.74 indices and repeated bit were visually checked; full arguments on pp.74–75 were read. Adopt only these repaired finite-extension arguments, without the subsequent forcing theory.
